newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW resume talks in Pontiac strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW resume talks in Pontiac strike.

text.p: Negotiators have resumed scheduled talks on Thursday aimed at resolving a two-day-old General Motors Corp pickup truck plant strike in Pontiac, Mich. a GM spokesman said.

About 5,800 members from United Auto Worker union Local 594 went on strike shortly before midnight April 22. The union members work at an assembly plant for GM's full-size pickup trucks in Pontiac, Mich., as well as related engineering and seat assembly operations.
UAW officials want GM to add up to 600 jobs to ease overtime burdens at the plant and address other health and safety issues.
Including the Pontiac strike, GM and Chrysler Corp are facing three UAW walkouts that have idled more than 33,000 workers in North America.
Most of those workers -- 21,868 -- have been idled at Chrysler facilities because of a strike by 1,800 employees at the automaker's Mound Road Engine Plant in Detroit. Talks continue in that dispute.
Talks are also continuing in Oklahoma City, Okla., where about 3,500 workers are on strike at a GM plant that makes the Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass. That strike began at midnight April 4.
